neighbours.label: ' $' before a price in commodity and market reports
fire: Crude oil for January delivery rose 90 cents. Brent crude closed at $82.40 a barrel on Thursday.
Corn futures gained 4 cents, while wheat for March delivery slipped to $6.15 a bushel in Chicago.
Aluminium edged up on the LME. Copper fell sharply, ending the session at $3.90 per pound.
Silver was down 20 cents, and spot gold climbed in London to settle near $1,945 an ounce.
Live hogs lost 2 cents. Feeder cattle contracts finished the week at $248 per hundredweight.
Prices for lint rose 3 cents this month, and the farmers sold their cotton crop for $0.71 a pound.
Heating oil eased 5 cents. Natural gas prices dropped to $2.55 per million British thermal units.
Coking coal held steady, and analysts expect iron ore to trade around $110 a tonne next quarter.
quiet: Crude oil for January delivery rose on supply worries. Brent crude closed sharply higher on Thursday.
Corn futures gained ground, while wheat for March delivery slipped in Chicago as rain eased drought fears.
Aluminium edged up on the LME. Copper fell sharply, ending the session at its lowest level since May.
Silver was weaker, and spot gold climbed in London as investors looked for safety.
Live hogs lost ground. Feeder cattle contracts finished the week near their record highs.
Prices for lint rose this month, and the farmers sold their cotton crop to a mill in the next county.
Heating oil eased slightly. Natural gas prices dropped as mild weather cut heating demand.
Coking coal held steady, and analysts expect iron ore to trade within a narrow range next quarter.

notes: Card: ' $' x6 and ' ' (space before a number) x7, in futures/commodity price reports. Probe: ' $' fires in multi-price commodity reports (0.89), not a lone retail price. Near misses keep the report with no dollar amount or number.
